questions.a: Restaurant business intelligence (BI) is the practice of collecting data from across your operation and turning it into information you can act on. It pulls together sales, labor, inventory, guest feedback and financials into a single view. That dashboard tells you what's happening, why it's happening and what to do about it.

questions.q: How does business intelligence help a restaurant make better decisions?
questions.a: BI connects data that normally sits in separate systems, so you can see the cause behind a number. If Friday dinner revenue drops, connected data might show slower ticket times from new menu items, more guest complaints about wait times and a line that's already well staffed. You'd fix the menu items instead of cutting staff, which would have made things worse.

questions.q: What data should restaurant BI software track?
questions.a: Most operators track five areas: guest experience, sales and revenue, labor, inventory and operations. Guest experience covers ratings, reviews and survey scores like NPS and CSAT. Operations can include safety audits and checklists, which show where standards slip across locations.

questions.q: Do I need separate BI software if my POS has reporting?
questions.a: Not always. Many POS systems include solid sales and menu reporting, which is often enough for an independent restaurant. Multi-unit groups usually add dedicated tools for labor, food cost or guest feedback, or a platform that combines data from several systems into one dashboard.

questions.q: How much does restaurant business intelligence software cost?
questions.a: Most BI and analytics tools for restaurants use custom pricing based on your number of locations, integrations and modules. Some labor tools offer a free plan for small teams, and POS reporting is often included in your POS subscription. Enterprise platforms for large groups are quoted individually.

questions.q: How can I measure guest satisfaction across my restaurants?
questions.a: Collect feedback from several channels, such as QR surveys, online reviews, email and SMS, then track it in one dashboard over time. Momos does this for restaurants, with sentiment analysis, NPS, CSAT and star-rating tracking, and alerts for low ratings and negative reviews. Its POS and reservation integrations tie satisfaction back to the actual dining experience.
